limitations: This verdict binds the independently reverified 62-file candidate only, on Linux x86_64 with LLVM/Clang 18, Bubblewrap 0.9.0, Python 3.12.3 and Node 22.23.3.

The independent neighbors performance run is a warm-cache local baseline with seven samples per case, not a cold-cache, large-production-project, or cross-platform benchmark. It measured linear query/connection growth for synthetic fanout but did not establish a contract-level performance failure.
Synthetic SQLite scale cases are not Clang semantic evidence; the performance run also included a real public CLI/new-analyzer/Bubblewrap multi-file case for semantic and readonly checks.
PCH/modules, complex full-program virtual dispatch, M2 incrementality/Git diff, private projects and large-scale performance remain outside M1 scope.

The first refresh harness was invalid because the two-index fixture could not expose a second page and the harness had route cleanup errors. It was not counted as product evidence; a replacement real 22-index Chromium harness produced the valid refresh result.
recommendation: ACCEPT. The refresh/history/selection race requirements and the prior M1 navigation/Unicode requirements are closed for this candidate. The user may approve freezing M1-Final. Treat the measured neighbors N+1 growth as a documented follow-up optimization candidate, not as a claim that query batching has already been implemented. No commit, push, merge, release or M2 action was performed by this audit.
